pages.text: Moe follows Oak, and he gets soaked.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy wading in, soaked

pages.text: Oak gets a gold bow for best float. Moe gets a hot bath at home.
pages.pictureBrief: The toad with a bow; the boy in a bath

readers.title: The Night the Lights Went Off

pages.text: It was late at night. A storm made the lights go off.
pages.pictureBrief: A dark house in a storm

pages.text: Mike did not like the dark. He held his flashlight tight.
pages.pictureBrief: A boy holding a flashlight

pages.text: Then a bright flash lit up the sky. Was it lightning? Mike felt a fright.
pages.pictureBrief: Lightning in the window

pages.text: But Dad sat with him and gave him pie.
pages.pictureBrief: Dad sitting with the boy, sharing pie

pages.text: "It is all right," Dad said. "The sun will be high in the morning."
pages.pictureBrief: Dad comforting the boy

pages.text: Mike gave a sigh and slept all night.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy asleep

pages.text: Kate has a kite with a bright tail.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl with a kite with a bright tail

pages.text: She takes it to the hill at first light.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl on a hill at sunrise

pages.text: The kite flies high in the sky.
pages.pictureBrief: The kite high in the sky

pages.text: Then the wind stops, and the kite dives down!
pages.pictureBrief: The kite diving

pages.text: It lands in a tree. Kate tries to get it, though it is very high.
pages.pictureBrief: The kite stuck in a tall tree

pages.text: Her dad helps, and they get it. "Let us try again tomorrow," says Kate.
pages.pictureBrief: Dad and the girl walking home with the kite

pages.text: Every Friday night, Gran makes a pie, and I help.
pages.pictureBrief: A grandma rolling dough

pages.text: Tonight, it is a peach pie.
pages.pictureBrief: A bowl of peaches

pages.text: I tie on my apron and get a big bowl.
pages.pictureBrief: A child tying an apron

pages.text: I help Gran slice the peaches.
pages.pictureBrief: The child slicing peaches

pages.text: The pie bakes, and the kitchen smells just right. I can not wait!
pages.pictureBrief: The pie in the oven

pages.text: We eat it by the light of the fire. It is the best night of the week.
pages.pictureBrief: The two eating pie by the fire

pages.text: Brook took a good book to the pool. It was a cookbook for kids.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl carrying a cookbook to a pool

pages.text: She read it on a stool in the cool shade of a tree.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl reading under a tree

pages.text: Soon she was in the mood for food.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl's tummy rumbling, picturing food

pages.text: At noon, she and her dad went to the kitchen. They put a scoop of rice in a pot of water.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl and her dad at the stove

pages.text: She stood by the pot with a big spoon. Stir, stir, stir!
pages.pictureBrief: The girl stirring

pages.text: The food was so good! Her brother took a look and had some too. "You are a good cook," he said.
pages.pictureBrief: Brother and sister eating together

pages.text: A moose and a goose live by a cool brook in the woods.
pages.pictureBrief: A moose and a goose beside a brook in the forest

pages.text: Each morning, the goose takes a bath in the brook. The moose stands on the shore and munches leaves.
pages.pictureBrief: The goose splashing; the moose eating leaves

pages.text: One day, the moose put his foot in deep mud. He could not move!
pages.pictureBrief: The moose stuck in mud

pages.text: "Help!" he called. The goose swooped down to look.
pages.pictureBrief: The goose flying down

pages.text: The goose pushed and pulled with all her might. Shoop! His foot came loose.
pages.pictureBrief: The goose tugging; the moose's hoof popping free

pages.text: "You are a good friend," said the moose. They had a snack of roots by the brook until the moon was up.
pages.pictureBrief: The two friends under the moon

pages.text: Whose shoe is this? It is in the brook!
pages.pictureBrief: A shoe floating in a little brook

pages.text: Luke looks. It is his school shoe!
pages.pictureBrief: A boy looking into the brook in surprise

pages.text: How did it get into the brook? Luke thinks and thinks.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy scratching his head

pages.text: He looks at his dog, Hoot. Hoot looks at the moon and wags his tail.
pages.pictureBrief: A dog looking innocent

pages.text: Luke gets a broom and hooks the shoe. He pulls it from the brook, and it drips on his foot.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy fishing the shoe from the brook with a broom

pages.text: Then he finds his other shoe in the dog bed, full of fur. "Hoot! You took my shoes!" Hoot just wags.
pages.pictureBrief: The dog in its bed beside a furry shoe

pages.text: Sue has a new blue suit. On Tuesday, she flew to see her nephew.
pages.pictureBrief: A woman in a blue suit on a plane

pages.text: She gave him fruit juice and a few clues for a game.
pages.pictureBrief: The woman giving a boy juice

pages.text: "Is it true that you grew?" said Sue. "You are so tall!"
pages.pictureBrief: The boy standing on tiptoe

pages.text: Her nephew just blew a bubble and chewed his stew. He did not say a thing.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy blowing a bubble at the table

pages.text: Then he drew a blue bird for Sue, with a big yellow beak.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy drawing a blue bird

pages.text: She will glue it in her book. "What a beautiful bird," said Sue. "What a beautiful day!"
pages.pictureBrief: The woman hugging her nephew with the drawing

pages.text: Drew and his crew are busy. They have a new boat.
pages.pictureBrief: A boy and his friends beside a small sailboat

pages.text: First, they need to fix a few screws and paint the deck blue. It is a lot of work.
pages.pictureBrief: The kids painting the deck

pages.text: Then Drew threw a rope to the crew, and they set sail.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy tossing a rope

pages.text: The wind blew, and the boat flew over the waves. Drew held on to the rail and grinned at his crew.
pages.pictureBrief: The boat skimming over waves

pages.text: At noon, the crew had fruit and hot stew on the deck. The sun was hot, and the sea was blue.
pages.pictureBrief: The kids eating on the deck

pages.text: "This is the best crew," said Drew. "You are true friends."
pages.pictureBrief: The crew grinning together

pages.text: June needs glue. Her paper bird has a broken wing.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl holding a paper bird with a broken wing

pages.text: She hunts in the kitchen. She hunts in her room. No glue.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl looking in kitchen drawers

pages.text: Is it in the hall? Is it on the shelf? Is it in the toolbox?
pages.pictureBrief: The girl searching a shelf and a toolbox

pages.text: No luck. June feels blue. She sits on the steps and sighs.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl slumped on the stairs

pages.text: At last, she finds it in her jacket. It was there all along! June has to grin.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl pulling glue from her jacket pocket

pages.text: June fixes the wing. Now her bird looks new again, and it is beautiful. She hangs it by the window.
pages.pictureBrief: The paper bird hanging in a sunny window

pages.text: At dawn, a hawk saw a fawn on the lawn.
pages.pictureBrief: A hawk on a branch watching a fawn

pages.text: The fawn gave a yawn and began to crawl under the fence.
pages.pictureBrief: The fawn crawling under a fence

pages.text: Its mother had taught it to be ready. It kept its head low.
pages.pictureBrief: The fawn hiding with its head down

pages.text: The weather was cool, and the fawn was as soft as a feather.
pages.pictureBrief: The fawn curled in the grass

pages.text: The hawk did not want a fight. It flew off to hunt for its breakfast instead.
pages.pictureBrief: The hawk flying away

pages.text: I saw it all from my window, and I had to draw it. It was the best morning of August.
pages.pictureBrief: A child drawing at a window

pages.text: It was Saturday morning. Paul wanted to make breakfast for his mom.
pages.pictureBrief: A boy in the kitchen early in the morning

pages.text: He spread jam on bread and got a glass of milk.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy spreading jam

pages.text: He brought it to her on a tray with a straw and a fresh daisy.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy carrying a tray with a daisy

pages.text: Then his foot caught on the rug!
pages.pictureBrief: The boy tripping

pages.text: Paul paused. The tray tipped, but he held it steady.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy balancing the tray

pages.text: Mom woke up and saw the tray. "I thought I would sleep in, but this is better!" she said, and she gave Paul a hug.
pages.pictureBrief: Mom in bed hugging the boy

pages.text: Shawn wants to wash his dog, Paws.
pages.pictureBrief: A boy with a bucket and a shaggy dog

pages.text: But Paws does not want a bath. He crawls under the bed and hides.
pages.pictureBrief: The dog hiding under the bed

pages.text: Shawn has a plan. He gets a treat, sits on the floor and waits.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy holding a treat, waiting

pages.text: Paws smells the treat. First his head peeks from under the bed. Then his paws. Then the rest of him.
pages.pictureBrief: The dog's nose and paws poking out

pages.text: Shawn catches him and puts him in the bath. Paws shakes. Splash!
pages.pictureBrief: The dog shaking water everywhere

pages.text: Shawn is soaked, but Paws is clean. "That was a lot of work for one bath," Shawn thought.
pages.pictureBrief: The soaked boy and the clean dog

pages.text: A brown mouse came out of its house. It found a coin on the ground.
pages.pictureBrief: A mouse finding a shiny coin

pages.text: "Wow!" it said in a loud voice.
pages.pictureBrief: The mouse holding up the coin

pages.text: The noise woke the owl in the tower. The owl flew down to look.
pages.pictureBrief: An owl swooping from a tower

pages.text: The mouse did not shout. It did not point.
pages.pictureBrief: The mouse frozen still

pages.text: It hid the coin in its mouth and crept round the flower pot without a sound.
pages.pictureBrief: The mouse tiptoeing around a flower pot

pages.text: The owl gave a frown and flew back up to its tower. The mouse took the coin home. What a proud mouse!
pages.pictureBrief: The mouse in its house with the coin

pages.text: A clown came to our town with a big brown cow.
pages.pictureBrief: A clown leading a brown cow into town

pages.text: The boys and girls gave a shout of joy.
pages.pictureBrief: Children cheering

pages.text: The clown made the cow bow. Then he made it spin round and round.
pages.pictureBrief: The cow bowing

pages.text: Then the cow sat down on the clown! The crowd gasped.
pages.pictureBrief: The cow sitting on the clown

pages.text: In a minute, the clown got out from under the cow and found his crown in the dirt.
pages.pictureBrief: The clown with a crooked crown

pages.text: "Is this part of the show?" a boy asked. "Yes!" said the clown, and the crowd howled with joy.
pages.pictureBrief: The crowd laughing; the clown bowing

pages.text: Roy has four coins. He can buy one toy at the shop.
pages.pictureBrief: A boy holding four coins in a toy shop

pages.text: He points at a toy cowboy. He points at a round ball that bounces.
pages.pictureBrief: A toy cowboy and a bouncy ball on a shelf

pages.text: Which one should he choose? Roy thinks for a minute.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy thinking

pages.text: He thinks about his sister, Joy. She is sick in bed with a sore throat.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl in bed with a scarf

pages.text: Then Roy has his answer. He buys a soft brown owl for Joy.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy buying a stuffed owl

pages.text: Joy hugs the owl and smiles. Roy feels proud. That was the best choice of all.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl hugging the owl; the boy smiling

pages.text: The knight had a knot in his sock and a crumb on his knee.
pages.pictureBrief: A friendly knight with a crumb on his knee

pages.text: He did not know how to knit, and he did not know how to write. But he could climb!
pages.pictureBrief: The knight puzzled by knitting needles

pages.text: One night, a lamb was stuck on a high rock.
pages.pictureBrief: A lamb on a rocky ledge at night

pages.text: The knight did not knock or wait. He began to climb.
pages.pictureBrief: The knight climbing the rock

pages.text: His wrist went numb, but he did not stop. He got the lamb in his arms and came down.
pages.pictureBrief: The knight carrying the lamb down

pages.text: Now the lamb will often listen for his knock at the gate.
pages.pictureBrief: The lamb waiting by a gate

pages.text: Wren wrote a note to her friend on the island.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl writing a note at a desk by the sea

pages.text: She wrapped it in paper and tied it with a knot. Then she wrote her name on the front.
pages.pictureBrief: The note rolled up and tied

pages.text: She put it in a bottle and threw it into the sea.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl throwing a bottle into the waves

pages.text: The waves took the bottle to the island. It landed on the sand.
pages.pictureBrief: The bottle washing up on an island beach

pages.text: Her friend knelt on the sand, picked it up and read it. Then he jumped up and waved at the sea.
pages.pictureBrief: A boy kneeling, reading the note

pages.text: It said: Come for lunch! I will make crumb cake. Do not be late! Love, Wren
pages.pictureBrief: The note with a drawing of a cake

pages.text: Knock, knock! Who is at the door?
pages.pictureBrief: A front door with a knock

pages.text: It is my friend Kim, with a lamb in her arms!
pages.pictureBrief: A girl at the door holding a lamb

pages.text: The lamb wriggles free and runs to the kitchen. Its little feet go tap, tap, tap.
pages.pictureBrief: The lamb running across the kitchen

pages.text: It knocks over a jar of crumbs and licks them off the floor.
pages.pictureBrief: The lamb licking crumbs from the floor

pages.text: Kim and I kneel down. I comb its wool, and it lies still on my knee.
pages.pictureBrief: Two kids kneeling, combing the lamb

pages.text: "I know a lamb should not be in a kitchen," says Kim. "But it often visits me, and I could not say no."
pages.pictureBrief: The girls laughing with the lamb between them

pages.text: Fern is the tallest girl in her class, and she is the kindest too. Her friend Ray is smaller, but he is the fastest runner in the school.
pages.pictureBrief: A tall girl and a smaller boy at school

pages.text: On the coldest day of winter, the pond froze. Ray wanted to be the first to skate on it.
pages.pictureBrief: A frozen pond

pages.text: He ran quickly onto the ice. His feet slid, and he fell with a thud. He felt helpless and sore.
pages.pictureBrief: The boy sliding and falling on the ice

pages.text: Fern did not panic. She went slowly and safely across the ice to help him up.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl stepping carefully across the ice

pages.text: She was so helpful! She held his arm, and they went back step by step. "You are the bravest friend I have," said Ray gladly.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl helping the boy off the ice

pages.text: Fern was thankful that he was not badly hurt. They went home early and had hot milk by the fire.
pages.pictureBrief: The two friends with mugs by a fire

pages.text: Our puppy, Pickles, is playful and hopeful. He is never still. He is the most restless puppy on our street.
pages.pictureBrief: A bouncy puppy

pages.text: At night, he whines and paces in the kitchen. The kitchen floor is spotless, but Pickles is not sleepy.
pages.pictureBrief: The puppy pacing in a dark kitchen

pages.text: Dad tried a softer bed. Mom tried a quieter clock. I sang him a song. Nothing worked, and we were all sleepless.
pages.pictureBrief: Dad with a dog bed, Mom with a clock

pages.text: Then I had a plan. I gave him my oldest sock, the one that smells like me.
pages.pictureBrief: A child holding out an old sock

pages.text: Pickles sniffed it slowly. Then he curled up with it, and he was still at last.
pages.pictureBrief: The puppy curled around the sock

pages.text: Now he sleeps peacefully every night, with his nose on the sock. A sock is a useful thing for a lonely puppy.
pages.pictureBrief: The puppy sleeping

pages.text: On Earth Day, our class went to the park to learn how to help the earth.
pages.pictureBrief: A class arriving at a park

pages.text: Our teacher gave us gloves and bags. "Be careful," she said. "Some trash is sharp."
pages.pictureBrief: The teacher handing out gloves

pages.text: We picked up cans, cups, wrappers and plastic bags. We were quickly busy, and the bags got heavy.
pages.pictureBrief: Kids picking up litter

pages.text: Then I heard a sad chirp in a bush. A little bird was stuck in a plastic ring. It could not fly.
pages.pictureBrief: A bird tangled in a plastic ring

pages.text: Our teacher carefully cut the ring, and the bird was free. It flew to a branch and sang loudly.
pages.pictureBrief: The bird singing on a branch

pages.text: We filled ten bags that day. Our park was spotless, and we felt hopeful and proud. Every day can be Earth Day.
pages.pictureBrief: Ten full bags and a clean park

pages.text: Dad had to unpack the van and unlock the shed. Mom had to preheat the oven and reheat the stew.
pages.pictureBrief: Dad unpacking, Mom at the oven

pages.text: My sister had to refill the dog dish. I had to redo my bed, and I dislike that job.
pages.pictureBrief: A child remaking a messy bed

pages.text: I was unhappy. I sat on the steps with my arms crossed and a frown on my face.
pages.pictureBrief: The child sulking on the steps

pages.text: Then Dad said we could replay our best game when we return from the market.
pages.pictureBrief: Dad holding up a board game

pages.text: I did not disagree! My sister is young, so we had to retell the rules twice.
pages.pictureBrief: Kids explaining rules to a little sister

pages.text: It was still fun to be a team. We finished every job by lunch. Redoing my bed was not so bad after all.
pages.pictureBrief: The family playing a game together

pages.text: Jade wrote a story about a young dragon who could not fly.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl writing about a little dragon

pages.text: She read it to her class, but she was unhappy with the ending. In her story, the dragon just sat on a rock and gave up.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl reading aloud, frowning

pages.text: "I will rewrite it," she said. She unzipped her bag and took out a pencil.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl unzipping her bag

pages.text: In the new ending, the dragon is unafraid. It flaps and flaps, and it rises over the country hills.
pages.pictureBrief: A dragon flying over green hills

pages.text: Jade reread her story. She fixed a few words and added a picture of the dragon. Now it was just right.
pages.pictureBrief: The girl reading her story, pleased

pages.text: She retold it to her class the next day, and they cheered. Her teacher asked if she could display it on the wall.
pages.pictureBrief: The story pinned to the class wall

pages.text: It was my birthday, and a big box sat on the table.
pages.pictureBrief: A big wrapped box on a table

pages.text: I untied the string and began to unwrap the box. My whole family was watching me.
pages.pictureBrief: A child untying the string

pages.text: Inside was a smaller box, wrapped in red paper. I opened that one too.
pages.pictureBrief: A smaller box inside the big one

pages.text: Inside was a smaller box, and a smaller one, and a smaller one! I began to giggle.
pages.pictureBrief: Boxes inside boxes

pages.text: My brother could not hide his grin. He had packed the boxes himself, one inside the other, just to tease me.
pages.pictureBrief: A big brother grinning

pages.text: At last, I found a tiny box. Inside was a ticket to the country show, with rides and games! I was not displeased at all. I gave my brother a big hug.
pages.pictureBrief: The child hugging the brother, holding a ticket

pages.text: The puppies were the happiest dogs at the party. They were running and hopping and digging in the garden, and they were having the best time.
pages.pictureBrief: Puppies playing at a garden party

pages.text: The biggest puppy grabbed a cake from the table and carried it off.
pages.pictureBrief: A puppy carrying a cake

pages.text: Mom was baking more, so she missed it. I tried to stop him, but he was faster than me. He zipped past my legs.
pages.pictureBrief: A child chasing the puppy

pages.text: He hurried under the table, wagging his tail and licking his lips.
pages.pictureBrief: The puppy under the table with the cake

pages.text: He looked so funny with icing on his nose that we all smiled. We could not be cross with him.
pages.pictureBrief: Everyone smiling at the puppy

pages.text: Then we gave the babies some cake too, and the hottest day of the summer got even nicer.
pages.pictureBrief: Babies and puppies with cake

pages.text: Last summer, we went swimming in the ocean. The water was colder than the pool, but I was hoping for big waves.
pages.pictureBrief: A family at the ocean

pages.text: My sister was digging in the sand and making a castle with a moat and a tiny flag.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl building a sand castle

pages.text: I was running and hopping over the little waves. Splash, splash! The water tickled my toes.
pages.pictureBrief: A child jumping over waves

pages.text: Then the biggest wave of the day splashed me, and I tumbled into the water.
pages.pictureBrief: A big wave knocking the child over

pages.text: I cried, but Dad carried me back to our towel and hugged me. He wrapped me up until I was warm.
pages.pictureBrief: Dad carrying the child

pages.text: Soon I was smiling again. We had the sunniest day, and it was a special day by the ocean.
pages.pictureBrief: The family on a towel at sunset

pages.text: On Sundays, Grandma and I spend the morning baking. Her kitchen always smells sweet, and she lets me put on her old apron.
pages.pictureBrief: A grandma and child in aprons

pages.text: Today we are making the tastiest muffins we have ever baked. Grandma says the secret is lots of berries.
pages.pictureBrief: A muffin tin on the counter

pages.text: First, I scooped the flour. Then I dropped in the berries, one by one. I only ate a few of them.
pages.pictureBrief: The child adding berries

pages.text: Grandma let me do the stirring. I stirred and stirred until my arm was tired.
pages.pictureBrief: The child stirring a big bowl

pages.text: While the muffins were baking, we hopped and twirled in the kitchen. Grandma is the silliest dancer I know.
pages.pictureBrief: Grandma and child dancing

pages.text: The muffins were the yummiest ever, with purple berries popping out the top. We saved the biggest one for Grandpa.
pages.pictureBrief: A plate of muffins

pages.text: Last year, we went to the city on a train. I bought a pencil and thought I would draw the square.
pages.pictureBrief: A family in a city square

pages.text: I could hear a whistle near the stairs. A chef in a tall white hat gave us fresh bread to share.
pages.pictureBrief: A chef handing out bread

pages.text: Then we saw the circus! A bear sat on a chair, and a giant did magic.
pages.pictureBrief: A circus with a bear on a chair

pages.text: A machine made a glowing ghost on a sign, and that gave me a scare.
pages.pictureBrief: A glowing ghost on a sign

pages.text: We were there for eight hours. My feet were sore, but I did not care one bit.
pages.pictureBrief: Tired family walking

pages.text: That night, I drew the city: the square, the chef, the bear and the ghost. It was my best picture all year.
pages.pictureBrief: A child's drawing of the city

pages.text: A bear lived near a fair in the hills. Every year, he could hear the music from his cave.
pages.pictureBrief: A bear listening from his cave

pages.text: One night, he thought he would go and see it. He went down the stairs of rock with care.
pages.pictureBrief: The bear walking down the rocky slope

pages.text: At the fair, there was a chair on a stage, and a sign that said: Rest Here.
pages.pictureBrief: A chair on a stage

pages.text: The bear sat on the chair. It gave a creak and broke in half! The people stared.
pages.pictureBrief: The chair breaking under the bear

pages.text: "I am sorry," said the bear. "To be honest, I only wanted to hear the music."
pages.pictureBrief: The bear looking sorry

pages.text: A kind girl gave him a pear and a big seat on the grass. The bear swayed to the music until the stars came out.
pages.pictureBrief: The bear swaying happily on the grass

pages.text: In a castle on a hill lived a gentle giant. He was eight times as tall as a man.
pages.pictureBrief: A giant beside a castle

pages.text: The people in the city were scared of him. Children ran when they heard his feet.
pages.pictureBrief: Children running

pages.text: But the giant only wanted a friend. He liked to whistle, to grow flowers and to bake bread.
pages.pictureBrief: The giant baking bread

pages.text: One day, a girl named Clair got lost in the forest near his castle. It was getting dark.
pages.pictureBrief: A girl lost among tall trees

pages.text: The giant heard her cry. He gently lifted her onto his hand and carried her home with care.
pages.pictureBrief: The giant carrying the girl

pages.text: After that, nobody in the city was scared of him. Clair came every week, and they shared the bread he baked.
pages.pictureBrief: The giant and girl sharing bread

pages.text: Our teacher gave us a mission: make an invention for the future.
pages.pictureBrief: A teacher at the board

pages.text: I drew a picture of a tricycle with a television on it, so I could watch shows as I rode. My friend made a unicorn that can sail.
pages.pictureBrief: Drawings of a tricycle and a unicorn sailboat

pages.text: Our mixture of glue and paint was terrible. It was sticky and lumpy, but at least it was washable.
pages.pictureBrief: Kids with paint and glue everywhere

pages.text: A visitor had a question. "Is this an adventure or an accident?"
pages.pictureBrief: A visitor raising an eyebrow

pages.text: It was possible that she was right! We looked at our sticky hands and laughed at the mess together.
pages.pictureBrief: The kids laughing

pages.text: Still, we felt the enjoyment and the kindness in the room, and that was the best part of the whole invention.
pages.pictureBrief: The class with their inventions

pages.text: On our vacation, we went on an adventure to a big park in the mountains.
pages.pictureBrief: A family car arriving at a park

pages.text: We rode our bicycles along a trail by a river. My little brother rode his tricycle, and he was the slowest, but he did not stop once.
pages.pictureBrief: A family on bikes on a trail

pages.text: At the station, a ranger told us about the creatures that live there.
pages.pictureBrief: A ranger talking to the family

pages.text: We saw a moose in motion, a turtle in the sunshine and a heron in the reeds.
pages.pictureBrief: A moose, a turtle and a heron

pages.text: Then the darkness came. We set up our tent, and I wore my warmest clothes.
pages.pictureBrief: A tent at dusk

pages.text: We sat by the fire and told stories. It was the best adventure of my life, and I want another one in the future.
pages.pictureBrief: The family by a campfire

pages.text: My sister is an artist. She painted a picture of a creature with three eyes and a long purple tongue.
pages.pictureBrief: A painting of a funny three-eyed creature

pages.text: Mom looked at it with confusion. "What is this creature?" she asked.
pages.pictureBrief: Mom puzzled

pages.text: "It is a friendly monster," said my sister. "It lives under the bed, and it eats bad dreams."
pages.pictureBrief: The creature under a bed

pages.text: I thought it was a wonderful invention. A monster who eats bad dreams would be very useful! I asked if it eats good dreams too. "No," she said. "Just bad ones."
pages.pictureBrief: A child smiling at the painting

pages.text: That night, my sister hung the picture above my bed. The creature looked kind, and I felt safe and calm.
pages.pictureBrief: The painting above a bed

pages.text: I slept the whole night with no bad dreams at all. Now I hope the creature stays with us forever.
pages.pictureBrief: A child sleeping peacefully
